sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Industrials lead a narrow field of three all-green sectors, while momentum remains fragile in Healthcare and Financials despite their recent gains.

Industrials is currently the standout leader of the market, serving as the only sector to be classified as "sustained strong" across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons. It sits at rank 2 with a top momentum score of 0.80. Technology also maintains strong momentum at 0.783, holding the number 1 YTD rank. Meanwhile, Healthcare is rotating upward, gaining one spot to reach rank 8 with 0.60 momentum.

Fading momentum is most visible in Energy and Financials, which both dropped one spot over the last five sessions to ranks 3 and 9, respectively. Consumer Cyclical remains the deepest laggard in the market, anchored at rank 11 with a weak momentum score of 0.283. 

## Strength
* **Narrow Breadth:** Only 3 of 11 groups are currently "all-green" (positive across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD): Industrials, Healthcare, and Financials.
* **Industrials Dominance:** Industrials is the sole "sustained strong" sector across 1-, 3-, and 6-month ranks, boasting the highest momentum score of 0.80.
* **Tech Holding Rank:** Technology maintains its YTD rank of 1 with a robust momentum score of 0.783, though it remains outside the all-green category.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Upward Shifts:** Healthcare (+1 spot to rank 8, 0.60 momentum) and Industrials (+1 spot to rank 2, 0.80 momentum) are the only sectors to improve their ranks over the last 5 sessions.
* **Rank Declines:** Energy (-1 spot to rank 3, 0.43 momentum) and Financials (-1 spot to rank 9, 0.53 momentum) are the week's top losers by rank.
* **Deep Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical (0.283 momentum, rank 11) and Consumer Defensive (0.300 momentum, rank 6) remain anchored at the bottom of the momentum curve.

## Divergences
* **Fragile All-Green Signals:** Despite their all-green status, Financials and Healthcare exhibit highly unstable ranks with very low agreement scores of 0.34 and 0.39, respectively.
* **Financials Disconnect:** Financials is technically all-green and a top momentum leader (0.533), yet it fell 1 spot to rank 9 this week with a fragile agreement score of 0.34.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** High-tech manufacturing and defensive healthcare maintain a firm grip on market leadership, while retail and commodities experience sharp weekly rotations out of favor.

The market shows healthy underlying breadth with 33 of 144 industry groups achieving "all-green" status, indicating positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons. Leadership remains highly concentrated in technology hardware and industrial capital goods, led by Semiconductor Equipment & Materials and Electronic Components. Healthcare Plans and Food Distribution also show sustained, multi-month strength, acting as reliable defensive anchors.

Conversely, consumer-facing sectors and cyclical commodities are undergoing a rapid cool-down. Apparel, Department, and Discount Stores all suffered steep rank declines this week, signaling a broad-based pullback in retail. Sellers also targeted Uranium and Aluminum, which fell sharply in the rankings, while early-stage momentum is beginning to build in select lagging areas like Auto Manufacturers and Education Services.

## Strength
* **Dominant Tech Hardware:** Semiconductor Equipment & Materials leads the entire market with a near-perfect momentum score of 0.985, closely followed by Electronic Components at 0.920. Both are sustained leaders across all timeframes.
* **Defensive and Industrial Anchors:** Healthcare Plans (0.880 momentum) and Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery (0.879 momentum) continue to show robust, all-green performance trends.
* **Broad-Based Breadth:** Nearly a quarter of the market (33 of 144 groups) is in a fully aligned uptrend, with Textile Manufacturing (0.816) and Food Distribution (0.810) among the highly rated all-green industries.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Rapid Climbers:** Health Information Services led all gainers, jumping 26 spots to rank 89 (0.60 momentum). Staffing & Employment Services (+24 spots to rank 54) and Silver (+22 spots to rank 66) also saw aggressive short-term bid interest.
* **Sharp Declines:** Apparel Retail plummeted 28 spots to rank 97 (0.31 momentum), matching a 28-spot drop for Uranium (rank 88, 0.28 momentum). Conglomerates (-26 spots) and Discount Stores (-25 spots) also experienced severe weekly distribution.
* **Persistent Laggards:** Utilities - Independent Power Producers (0.097 momentum) and Paper & Paper Products (0.113 momentum) remain anchored to the bottom of the YTD rankings with virtually no signs of recovery.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leadership:** Several high-momentum groups are beginning to stall out and slip in rank, including Scientific & Technical Instruments (0.78 momentum, -1 spot), Semiconductors (0.71 momentum, -1 spot), and Engineering & Construction (0.70 momentum, -3 spots).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Auto Manufacturers jumped 15 spots to rank 115 despite a mediocre 0.50 momentum score. Similarly, Education & Training Services gained 12 spots with a momentum score of just 0.46, indicating early-stage accumulation in beaten-down groups.
